title: Module 9 · Lesson 3 — Privacy, audit and governance

lines: Welcome to Module Nine, Lesson Three: privacy, audit, and governance.
You're tested on the engineering side of the rules, not legal detail.
Picture BrightLoan, an online lender whose agent pre-screens loan applications.
Then three hard questions arrive.

say.0: Picture Bright Loan, an online lender whose agent pre-screens loan applications.

lines: An applicant wants their data erased, and a regulator asks why a March application was declined.
An auditor asks if the agent is fair to every group.
Privacy starts with minimisation: send only the fields the model needs.
Redact or tokenise personal details before they reach a model or a log.
If data can't leave, self-host the model with NIM.
And limit how long prompts, traces, and memory are kept.
An erasure request must reach every copy.
The vector index, memory, traces, and caches, not just the main database.
The regulator needs an audit trail, which is not application logging.
It's immutable, tamper-evident, access-controlled, and retained per policy.
It records the input, who asked, the sources, and every tool call with its arguments and result.
Plus approvals, the output, and the exact model, prompt, and policy versions.
With that record, BrightLoan can reconstruct the March decision.
That's the answer the regulator wants.

say.0: With that record, Bright Loan can reconstruct the March decision.

lines: Credit is high-risk under the EU AI Act, which tiers obligations by risk.
High-risk uses need human oversight, logging, transparency, documentation, and conformity assessment.
NIST's AI Risk Management Framework has four functions: govern, map, measure, manage.
ISO/IEC 42001 is certifiable, and model cards document intended use and limits.

say.1: I S O, I E C forty-two thousand and one is certifiable, and model cards document intended use and limits.

lines: Then fairness: the agent is ninety-two percent accurate overall.
Split by subgroup, one group fares far worse.
Bias enters through data, retrieval, prompts, and majority-only test sets.
So evaluate by subgroup, audit sources, red-team with varied inputs, and offer an appeal path.
On the exam, regulated data plus an outside model API means redact at the boundary, or self-host.
A contract alone isn't an engineering control, so read on.
